title: How to start investing with just $10 or $20 per week
description: Building a six-figure portfolio using the 'Latte Factor' budget.
content:
The most common excuse for not investing is 'I don't have thousands of dollars.' This excuse is obsolete. In the modern era of fractional shares and zero-commission trading, the mathematical barrier to entry is literally $1. Investing $20 a week—the price of one fast-food meal—can grow into a substantial nest egg over time. The key is not the amount, but the velocity (frequency) and duration (time). This guide shows how micro-contributions create macro results.

Key Takeaways

  • The Rule of 72: At 10% returns, your money doubles every 7.2 years. Even small amounts compound massively over 40 years.
  • Consistency > Intensity: Investing $20 every single week is better than investing $1,000 once and forgetting about it. It builds the identity of an investor.
  • Dollar Cost Averaging: Buying small amounts weekly ensures you buy more shares when the market is down, lowering your average cost automatically.
  • Avoid Fees: With small amounts, you MUST use a free broker (Fidelity/Robinhood). Paying a $5 fee on a $20 investment is a 25% loss instantly.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The S&P 500 has historically returned ~10% annually. If you invest $20/week ($86/mo) from age 20 to 65 at 10%, you end up with Over $750,000. That is the power of starting young with small amounts.

The $20/Week Roadmap

How to turn pocket change into a portfolio.

Step 1: The Platform

You need a brokerage that supports Fractional Shares and Recurring Investments.

  • Fidelity: Allows $1 fractional buys. Excellent for Roth IRAs.
  • Robinhood: extremely user-friendly for setting up recurring buys.
  • SoFi: Great for automating transfers from checking.

Step 2: The Asset

With $20, you can't diversify by buying 10 different stocks. Buy one ETF that holds everything.

Ticker: VTI (Total US Stock Market) or VT (Total World Stock).

Why? You own Apple, Microsoft, and 3,000 other companies for $20. If one goes bust, you don't care.

Step 3: The Setup

Don't rely on memory. Set it to pull $20 every Monday morning. Make it invisible. Treat it like a Netflix subscription you can't cancel.

Scaling Up

  1. The 1% Raise: When you get a raise at work, increase the weekly auto-buy by $5. You won't feel it, but it accelerates the compounding.
  2. The 'Found Money' Rule: If you find $20 in an old coat or get a $20 refund, manually deposit it. Train your brain to see found money as investment capital, not spending money.
  3. Dividend Reinvestment (DRIP): Ensure this setting is ON. When your $20 worth of stock pays a $0.10 dividend, use it to buy $0.10 more stock. This is the turbocharger.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it worth it for such a small amount?

Yes. The first $1,000 is the hardest. Once you see the balance grow to $500, then $1,000, your psychology changes. You will naturally find ways to save more.

Should I buy Crypto with my $20?

Maybe $1 of it (5%). But $19 should go to the S&P 500. Crypto is a lottery ticket; Stocks are an ownership stake in the economy. Build the foundation first.

Can I withdraw it?

Yes, but don't. This is for 'Future You'. If you treat it like a piggy bank, it will never grow. Forget the password if you have to.
